title: nbn FTTP or HFC 1000/100 $99/Month Ongoing (New Customers) @ Superloop
body:
Deal: nbn FTTP or HFC 1000/100 $99/Month Ongoing (New Customers) @ Superloop

[Winny182] You’re literally posting 4 cheaper deals in the description?
[bcYield] Flat Vs Churn
They do this like what they did at Exetel
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/913142
[Wiadro] So there’s cheaper options and you post this?
$99 is their usual price for customer retention after any cheaper offer.
[bcYield] It's not. They told me the discount for customer retention would be expired and required another call. If $99 is the usual price, it would destroy the purpose of this new deal.
[Wiadro] I don’t think you understand
Anytime I have been a cheaper 1000/100 on SL than $99 eg $79 or $89 for 6 months
After that 6 months it would goto $109 or recently $114, I would call up and say I want to cancel and they would always offer the same plan for $99.
The only thing is here it’s $99 until they feel like changing the t&c
[Xizor] They didnt with me (to my surprise). That said service/performance night and day better on Leaptel and Neptune which have seen bounced through.
[bcYield] Yes they do applying a discount with an expiry for you. Mine will be expired by the next month or so. The rep told me this. That's how it works. Initially I had thought the same until I discussed it with them.
[Wiadro] @bcYield: So they aren’t repeating the $99 offer anymore after the first time?
[bcYield] @Wiadro: They want us to call them again by the time it's expired. It can take half an hour easily for a call. This flat rate deal can remove the unnecessary call.
[bogak] @bcYield: They stopped it that for me after the 3rd time. They said sorry no more discount, so I left. The 6 month discount is not forever even if you ring them and ask for it.
[Wiadro] @bcYield: That’s why you churn from SL to SL and get a better price
[WaveZero] Superloop support has gone downhill. They cannot listen to basic instructions or do anything unless you raise a TIO. My parents had issues with their NBN, and NBN kept rescheduling at 2-3 a.m. Superloop kept blaming my parents because they marked the appointment as attended premises and no one was at home. I kept explaining that it is impossible for the NBN subcontractors to visit in the middle of the night, but they kept saying it was our fault. The NBN subbie did this for an entire month, probably abusing the call-out fee or whatever. I told Superloop to escalate with NBN on multiple occasions, raised a few complaints through their official complaint email, and called multiple times. The issue is that they have basically offshored all their support overseas, and those support reps lack common sense. They even messed up the pro-rata refund. I've cancelled all my services with them.
[Avalanche] Totally agree on this. Their customer service have absolutely no common sense and no consistency as well. Depending on who you talk to the answer will vary. Just got my billing issue resolved with them after raising with TIO. Even their stupid 24 month free router logic is flawed where they started billing me from 3rd Dec 2024 but dispatched the router on the 3rd, so for completing 24 months for free router they needed me to stay till 3rd Dec 2026 while my plan expires on 2nd Dec 2026. If I end my plan on 2nd Dec they said I would be charged early cancellation fee. So had to again threaten them with another TIO complaint post which they credited the future penalty charge to my bill to offset the penalty. Never again with them
[arcticmonkey] I hate offshoring. They almost always don't have a clue, stick to templates and have no empowerment. Plus the god awful fake accents with some of them.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] I have found superloop amazing and super progressive. Their ai chatbot customer support does everything I need in seconds.
[OzViper] "I'm sorry Dave, I'm afraid I can't do that.."
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Lol. I got down voted for saying I have 10/10 experiences with this company? 😂
[Mellows] I'm the same. Been with Superloop for years. Rock solid connection, zero dropouts and the few times I had to ring customer care due to router issues they were great.
[Duala] My experience with Superloop was an absolute nightmare. Their AI chatbot falsely confirmed my NBN connection had been arranged, despite being unable to actually process the request. They then ignored my explicit instructions to provision FTTP only, resulting in conflicting orders, failed appointments and significant delays Customer service was pathetic with repeated misinformation and no accountability. We eventually had to escalate to the Ombudsman to recover our out-of-pocket expenses. Even cancelling the service was a nightmare. Despite providing a month's notice, superloop continued charging us. It took another threat of escalation to the Ombudsman before they finally relented. Others experience may be different but for me, never again.
[ad62623] Avoid. You should never be forced to explain yourself when cancelling a service.
[yellah] Any good opticom deals with a static IP?
[mickeyjuiceman] Superloop = stay away. Terrible support, and a 30-day notice required to escape the contract. i.e. years and years behind the times.
